arguments.summary:
A critical lateral movement incident was detected originating from external IP 45.33.32.156, which conducted an Nmap SYN scan against internal asset WS-IT-101 (10.0.2.15). The compromised host was subsequently used to authenticate to the 10.0.12.0/24 subnet under the context of user CORP\helpdesk. The svc_backup service account was identified as a potential vector and was immediately reset. Post-incident hardening was applied to WS-IT-101 via Ansible. Notably, EDR/NDr, sandboxing, and firewall reconfiguration proposals were rejected due to lack of consensus, indicating potential gaps in automated response policy.

Asset inventory and firewall policy context have been embedded for CISO review: All hosts in scope were within expected configurations, though segmentation rules did not explicitly deny east-west traffic to the 10.0.12.0/24 subnet, allowing lateral movement post-initial compromise.

timeline.description: External IP 45.33.32.156 initiated Nmap SYN scan targeting 10.0.2.15 (WS-IT-101). Detected and logged by IDS with low severity.
Successful internal authentication from 10.0.2.15 to 10.0.1.1 using CORP\helpdesk credentials. Lateral movement into 10.0.12.0/24 subnet initiated.
UEBA analysis returned low risk score (0.35) for svc_backup account; no behavioral anomalies detected.
SIEM correlation confirmed 23 events linking origin IP to lateral movement attempts under svc_backup context.
Service account 'svc_backup' password and MFA token reset via IAM/PAM integration. Secure enrollment link issued.
Ansible playbook 'linux_workstation_hardening.yml' successfully executed on WS-IT-101 to apply security baselines.
Firewall rule update and EDR containment actions rejected by consensus engine (2/4 approvals). No network isolation performed.
